name: cloud_underlight
description: §23 cloud-base underlighting (issue #88 option 1): the off/on true-no-op invariant (off must read exactly 1.0, the multiplier's neutral value — see CloudUnderlightProbe's own note on why the flag is checked directly rather than leaning on CloudAltitudeMetresFor's zero return) plus issue #88's headline opposite-sign invariant, using two REAL installed WeatherDefs and no custom Def: Overcast classifies dry (WeatherDimmingMath's automatic altitude classifier lands it at the 4000 m default — the table's 'mid altocumulus' row) and Sandstorm classifies fully precipitating (1000 m default — the table's 'low stratus' row). Latitude 45, day 40, sunset located by survey (civil dusk falls between hour 20.5 and 21 on this tile/season — see the parent CLAUDE.md's 'survey before you pick an hour' note). Hour 20.80 (sun elevation -1.49°, pinned live) is the point the survey found where the two decks' multipliers sit on opposite sides of 1.0: Overcast's shadow-entry angle (~2.03° at 4000 m) still has the deck lit and glowing, Sandstorm's (~1.02° at 1000 m) has already gone dark and is suppressing the tail — but the two phases are NOT symmetric (GlowPhase peaks fast and Sandstorm's own suppression window is barely 10% travelled at this exact elevation), so this crossover pair is the correctness demonstration, not the strongest visual one. A third pair at hour 20.95 (elevation -3.86°) is Sandstorm well past its own shadow entry, deep enough into its suppression window to be issue #88's 'kills the sunset' case at near-maximum strength on this tile. All probe values are exact live measurements, pinned per the parent CLAUDE.md rule (never replace a measured pin with a computed one) — a formula or classifier-default change invalidates the ladder and it must be re-run, not re-derived.
